initial_unbounded_launch_experiment.change: Kernel arithmetic/layout unchanged; final declaration adds __launch_bounds__(128), matching every actual launch. Initial benchmark compares explicit groups only, with no automatic selection.
initial_unbounded_launch_experiment.kernel_reproduction: Remove __launch_bounds__(128) and its two immediately preceding explanatory comment lines from the final kernel header. SHA256 is checked against the captured initial kernel source.

method: Each final workload fixes m, table/filter format, target set and scalar interval; group 1, group 8 and auto owners each have one warm-up plus five rotating-order samples.
All results checked for expected full-point matches, exact target giant-step count, no overflow, and CPU verification. Warm-up samples are retained as sample -1 but excluded from statistics.

Rates divide by submit-to-take wall time. Actual target giant steps/s counts each target row. Effective scalar-range coverage/s credits the interval once after all targets and is not literal public-key evaluations/s.
Build/upload/preparation are separate cold single observations, not repeated bandwidth estimates. Search timing excludes persistence; no durable coverage.
No power, clocks, partition or NUMA settings changed. Shared host, current CPU affinity retained. Snapshots bracket the experiments, not per-kernel telemetry.

Input JSON SHA256 uses sorted keys and compact separators; target digests use the production bsgs-targets-v1 domain over sorted native-oracle SEC1 points. Cache checksum is reproduced with the deterministic CPU builder.
Compiler resource estimates are not measured occupancy. SGPR spills and scratch remain after VGPR spills are eliminated.
Only SPX/NPS1 hardware was available. Auto uses visible CUs; actual CPX/QPX search performance/correctness remains unmeasured.
